newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland may act to ease fuel shortages - minister.
newsitem.headline: Poland may act to ease fuel shortages - minister.

text.p: Poland, with its fuel market hit by high world oil prices, may have to use state reserves of diesel and introduce duty-free import quotas to offset shortages, a deputy industry minister said on Wednesday.

Roman Czerwinski told a parliamentary economic committee that duty-free import quotas for 300,000 tonnes of gasoline and 400,000 tonnes of diesel may be needed the stabilise the market unless world oil prices fall.
"The situation on the engine fuels market cannot be regarded as stable, especially that a season of intensive agricultural work is underway," Czerwinski said.
"Opening the reserves and possibly duty-free import quotas would ensure stable deliveries to the market," he added.
He said the state-owned distribution company CPN SA had reserves of 91,400 tonnes of gasoline and 19,400 tonnes of diesel, which could ensure continuous supplies for 10 and three days respectively.
Reserves in the private sector were not known.

The government has already unveiled plans to introduce a duty-free import quota for 300,000 tonnes of gasoline but says the final decision when to launch it will be synchronised with a planned liberalisation of fuel prices.
Polish fuel prices are set by the finance ministry, which recently refused to increase them so as to avoid contributing to inflation.
But refineries and distributors, facing official caps on fuel prices and high prices of crude oil, find production and sales increasingly less profitable.
Czerwinski quoted CPN figures as showing that the current oil price of $219 a tonne would require that a litre of diesel fuel cost 1.53 zlotys to make sales profitable.
A litre of diesel from an import duty-free quota should cost 1.37 zlotys, while the official price is now 1.22 zlotys.
